Boot size 156W: EU 42-47 / US 9-12 / Mondo 27-30cm [2] 111. Core material: Light Core — 50/50 blend of Paulownia and Poplar [1][2] 112. Core difference vs standard Disaster: Standard Disaster uses full Poplar core with beech hardwood reinforcement; Disaster+ gets the lighter "Light Core" [26][34] 113. Fiberglass type: Bi-Ax (biaxial) laminate [1][2] 114. Carbon stringers: Yes — strategically placed to fine-tune flex, response and feel [1][2] 115. Carbon technology: C.S.T. SuperTubes — Central Super Tube, a single hollow carbon cylinder running down the center of the board [1][2] 116. C.S.T. function: Enhances pop without stiffening the board torsionally; reduces weight [2][35] 117. Aramid reinforcement: Aramid X-Ply — diamond weave laminate reinforced by Kevlar [1][2] 118. Aramid X-Ply function: Full perimeter 3D reinforcement providing exceptional torsional stability and improved damping [2] 119. Aramid X-Ply exclusivity: Exclusively featured in Bataleon's Plus Series [2] 120. Sidewall material: Flex Walls — Urethane Poured Sidewalls [1][2] 121. Sidewall function: Exceptional shock absorption, reduced chatter and vibration [2] 122. Base material: Hyper Glide S — standard sintered base [1][2] 123. Base description: Durable and fast; faster when kept waxed [2] 124. Edge material: Not explicitly specified; standard steel edges 125. Topsheet: New shape marked on manufacturer site for 2025/26 [2] 126. Pro rider association: Mikey B. [1][24] 127. Riding focus: Park, jib, rails [1] 128. Terrain focus: Park-dominant; some resort versatility [36][37] 129. Target rider level: Intermediate to Advanced (merchant-verified) [1]; "Advanced" per some sites [4] 130. Turning ease: Extremely easy to turn — "just have to think about turning and it does" [38] 131. Slow speed maneuverability: Ultra nimble edge-to-edge [38] 132. Edge catch resistance: One of the least catchy boards available — 3BT dramatically reduces edge catches [38][39] 133. Buttering/pressing: Effortless pressing and buttering capability [40][33] 134. Pop quality: Surprisingly good nose and tail pop from C.S.T. SuperTubes despite soft flex [33][35] 135. Carving performance: Poor — board wants to skid/let go at speed during carves [38][41] 136. High speed stability: Poor — gets chattery at higher speeds, unstable [42] 137. Big jump suitability: Not suited to bigger jumps; softness reduces stability on landing [33][38] 138. Small/medium jump suitability: Good for small to medium jumps [38] 139. Powder performance: Average at best; centered twin limits float [38][41] 140. Weight feel: Feels light on snow despite being average weight on scales; soft boards feel lighter [38] 141. Base speed: Notably fast sintered base; fastest jib board base per Board of the World [21][43] 142. Catch-free on rails: 3BT and SideKick technology keeps contact points from catching on jib features [43] 143. Rail lockdown: Excellent rail stability; "locks down on rails" [42] 144. Board of the World rating: 84.75/100 (4.24/5) [31] 145. Board of the World ranking: 27th out of 36 boards in park category [31] 146. Bataleon.com user reviews: 199 reviews, 92% 5-star [2] 147. The Inertia award: "Best Jib Board" in their 2026 best snowboards test [36] 148. Whitelines Disaster reviews: Selected for "Whitelines 100" best snowboard gear awards in 2020/21 and 2021/22 seasons [44][45] 149. SnowboardingProfiles.com Disaster+ review: "super fun, playful board that allows you to get all kinds of creative" [39] 150. SnowboardingProfiles.com summary: Not a one-board quiver; best as a park/freestyle board, complement with something for speed/carving/powder [39] 151. User review (Bataleon.com): "the disaster+ is the most fun and most unique board I've rode in a while" [33] 152. User review (Bataleon.com): "this board is so light, tricks of any kind are a breeze and yet to me the board does not feel like it will break" [33] 153. User review (Bataleon.com): "Super Tubes gives it a surprising amount of tail and nose pop" [33] 154. User review (Bataleon.com): "near impossible to catch an edge" with 3BT [33] 155. User review (Snowboarding Forum): "Build quality 10/10 — Bataleon always seems to have a really high build quality" [42] 156. Review consensus: Excellent for jibbing, pressing, buttering, creative park riding; very forgiving [36][39][43] 157. Indoor park suitability: Excellent for rope tow and indoor parks due to fast base in slow snow conditions [43] 158. User complaint (Bataleon.com Disaster reviews): "A bit too soft for me.. no pop!" (standard Disaster, not Plus) [46] 159. User complaint (forum): One user asked "does this board suck?" suggesting it doesn't suit all riders [47] 160. Carving limitation: Universally noted as poor at high-speed carving [38][41] 161. Powder limitation: Not suited for powder riding [38][41] 162. 3BT learning curve: 3BT is "an acquired taste" and you "drive it different than any other profile" — some forum users recommend against learning on 3BT [48] 163. 3BT polarization: Some riders don't enjoy 3BT — one rider reported his Evil Twin "gathers dust" [49] 164. Speed stability: Gets chattery and unstable at high speeds [42] 165. Not a one-board quiver: Most reviewers recommend pairing with a stiffer all-mountain board [39][46] 166. Weight (standard Disaster, older model): Forum noted the standard Disaster as "pretty heavy" for a jib board; the Plus version addresses this with lighter core [42] 167. Price premium: Costs approximately $94-$130 more than average snowboard/standard Disaster [21][31] 168. Comparable products — jib category: Capita Horrorscope, GNU Head Space, Ride Twinpig [50][51] 169. Comparable products — all-mountain freestyle with 3BT: Bataleon Evil Twin / Evil Twin+ (stiffer, more all-mountain versatile) [52] 170. Evil Twin+ comparison: Evil Twin+ ranked 1st/36 park boards by Board of the World; Disaster+ ranked 27th. Evil Twin+ is more versatile but less jib-specific [53] 171. CAPiTA DOA as alternative: User switched from Disaster to DOA and preferred it for all-around park use [54] 172. Ride Twinpig comparison: Twinpig is wider/shorter, also playful and pressable but with hybrid camber rather than 3BT [50] 173. Standard Disaster (non-Plus) comparison: Standard has softer flex (2/10), full Poplar core (heavier), no carbon stringers, no C.S.T., no Aramid X-Ply; saves ~$130 [26][34] 174. Standard Disaster price (evo): $499.95 USD [20] 175. Bataleon Wallie comparison: Wallie has carbon additives around center/inserts; slightly different construction approach [28] 176. 3BT Triple Base Technology: Positive camber from nose to tail with lifted sidebase contact points reducing edge catches [2][16] 177. 3BT Jib tune: Widest centerbase in the range for locked-in presses, least sidebase uplift [55] 178. SideKick technology: Amplifies sidebase uplift at the widest points of nose and tail, giving tips hull-like shape [2] 179. SideKick benefit: Enhanced float in deep snow; smoother turn initiation; edge-to-edge transitions [2] 180. Construction method: Sandwich construction with urethane sidewalls [2] 181. Binding compatibility: 2x4 insert pattern, compatible with any standard or mini disc binding [1] 182. Gender: Listed as men's / unisex — standard Disaster available in Men's, Women's and unisex versions; Disaster+ typically listed under men's [2][56] 183. Brand perception: Bataleon is well-respected for innovation, quality construction, and rider-driven design [57][58] 184. Brand loyalty: Many Bataleon riders are loyal repeat customers due to 3BT [59] 185. Build quality reputation: "Bataleon always seems to have a really high build quality. No flaws anywhere" [42] 186. Brand heritage: Over 20 years of 3D snowboard tech innovation with patented Triple Base Technology [16] 187. Factory quality: The Mothership is "the world's first snowboard manufacturing facility powered by 100% clean energy" [60] 188. Mothership sustainability: Carbon-neutral, hydro-powered, wood off-cuts used as heating [60][61] 189. Graphic style: Clean, relatively simple design aesthetic [62] 190. Base colour: Solid colour base (potentially faster due to smoother surface) [43] 191. New shape indicator: 2025/26 manufacturer page indicates "New shape" [2] 192. Disaster+ vs Disaster price delta at evo (2026 model): $629.95 vs $499.95 = $130 difference [18][20] 193. Disaster+ in bundles: Available as package with Blaster Pro AW Fase bindings at evo for $1,019.90 [63] 194. Comparable pricing of Evil Twin+ (Bataleon): $620-650 USD [53] 195. Edge hold limitation: Forum users note edge hold washes out on ice for soft Bataleon boards [42]
